night-notice-2.displayName: Second Text on the Night Limits Band

display.purpose: The project page's headline. One per page, never above 6rem.

handbook-display.purpose: The book title on the handbook's station band.

headline.purpose: Section headings on the project page, balanced across lines.

handbook-headline.purpose: Home headings in the handbook, each under a 1.5px ink rule.

title.purpose: Headings inside a section, and the book's section headings under a 1.5px ink rule.

item-title.purpose: Entries in a list: module names, re-entry phrases, research domains, lesson and case titles.

lede.purpose: The paragraph under a headline, in second ink.

body.purpose: Running text on the project page; 15px at 760px and below.

reading.purpose: The handbook's text at a 38em measure; the reader can choose 16, 17 or 19px and a Song body.

control.purpose: Bar links, tabs, small signs and compact buttons; at 400 it carries leg names, statuses and footers.

label.purpose: The label inside a ruled cell and the cell label of a stacked table. Never above a heading.

cell-value.purpose: The value under a cell label in a ruled strip.

sign.purpose: Lettering on direction signs, plain signs and plaques.

designator.purpose: R1 to R7, M0 to M9, part and strip numbers, versions, dates and counts, in tabular numerals.

numeral.purpose: The yellow numerals of the install steps; the 404 on both not-found pages runs up to 6rem in cobalt.

quotation.purpose: The quoted passage on the project page's source band, in XK Song.

handbook-quotation.purpose: The opening paragraph on the handbook home, in the reader's installed Song.

mono.purpose: File names, commands, topic and task identifiers.

chart-code.purpose: Fix and runway designators on the plan and the profile.

chart-name.purpose: Fix names on the plan and the profile.

chart-note.purpose: Notes, feeder labels and hazard notes on the drawings.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for state changes, panels, sheet turns and the chart's arrival. `--ease` on the project page, `--xk-ease` in the handbook.

motion.name: ease-in
motion.purpose: The outgoing sheet number when a sheet turns. `--xk-ease-in`.

motion.name: quick
motion.purpose: Hover, pressed and selected colour changes. `--xk-quick`; .16s on the project page.

motion.name: nudge
motion.purpose: The 2 to 3px icon nudge inside a hovered sign or link.

motion.name: panel
motion.purpose: Drawers, bay folds, switch thumbs and answer disclosures. `--xk-panel`; chevrons on the project page turn in 260ms.

motion.name: turn
motion.purpose: A sheet turn, a lesson fold and the rack holder's travel. `--xk-turn`.

motion.name: chart-arrival
motion.value: 950ms field rise, 700ms fades from 120ms and 300ms, fixes pop 520ms from 360ms at 55ms intervals, labels at 680ms, go-around at 820ms
motion.purpose: The plan view assembles once when the page loads.

motion.name: route-flight
motion.value: min(3600ms, 900ms + 2ms per unit of route length), quadratic ease-in-out
motion.purpose: The magenta route is drawn and the aircraft follows it; the first flight starts 1150ms after load.

motion.name: hold-circuit
motion.purpose: The aircraft flies one circuit of the hold when 60% of the drawing is in view.

motion.name: rose-settle
motion.purpose: The book rose turns into place once on arrival.

motion.name: sheet-turn
motion.value: old sheet 250ms fade with 320ms slide of 28px; new sheet 250ms fade with 440ms slide of 40px
motion.purpose: Moving between handbook sheets, from the side the new sheet lies on in the book; bar, rack and outline stay put.

motion.name: sheet-number
motion.purpose: The sheet number on the page strip rolls when the sheet turns.

motion.name: theme-spread
motion.value: 620ms cubic-bezier(.3, .1, .2, 1), circular clip from the switch
motion.purpose: Switching between the day and the night chart in the handbook.

motion.name: figure-zoom
motion.purpose: A figure grows into the lightbox and back.

motion.name: structure-cycle
motion.purpose: The structure drawing on the handbook home; paused when out of view or hidden.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The route is painted complete, the aircraft is parked, the structure drawing holds still, sheets change at once.

narrative.overview:
These eight sections define the two public web surfaces of the Xikari Skill as one system. The project page (`docs/index.html`, `docs/404.html`, `docs/assets/project.css`, `docs/assets/project.js`) draws the Skill as an approach plate: a question enters at the chart edge, flies a published route through numbered fixes, reaches a decision point, and either lands on RWY 09 as a written judgment or goes around. The handbook (theme in `website/.vitepress/theme/`, built to `docs/handbook/`) is the manual behind that chart: the book is the station every route is measured from, and each of its sheets is a flight progress strip, read in order. Theory text, Skill semantics and the pages the Skill generates are outside these sections; the generated pages keep their own system under Output surfaces.

The material is print. White chart paper, blue-black procedure ink in three strengths, a cobalt airspace tint, and flat page-wide fields of yellow, ink and cobalt. Data sits in ruled cells. A line's style states what kind of thing it draws: solid for what is required or sourced, dotted or short-dashed for what is conditional or assumed, long dashes for the go-around. Three signals are rationed by job: magenta says where the route or the reader is, yellow is the sign to act on or the one sentence to notice, red is a refusal. Nothing casts a shadow, nothing fades into anything else, and no control is rounded past 3px.

Both surfaces print a day chart and a night chart from the same roles. The project page is dense and declarative, made to be scanned once and acted on. The handbook is set for long continuous Chinese reading, so the chart vocabulary moves to the edges of the sheet (the strip rack, the page's own strip, the position rose) and the text column stays plain.
keyCharacteristics: One chart system across the project page and the handbook, in a day and a night printing.
Ruled strips for identity, status and navigation: label over value, 1px rules, a 1.5px ink frame.
Line style carries state, always with a legend or a tag beside it.
Magenta for position, yellow for the sign, red for refusal; cobalt for structure and links.
A heavy sans for titles, signs and designators; Song for the book's quoted words; monospace for identifiers.
Flat fields, square frames, no shadows.
Drawings are generated from data published on the page and recomposed for the space they have.
Motion answers an action: a route is flown, a sheet turns, a lesson folds.

rules.name: The Position Rule
rules.body: Magenta answers one question: where. It is a mark (a line, a fix, a holder, a marker bar, a focus ring), never a band, a button or a heading.

rules.name: The Sign Rule
rules.body: Yellow is a ground under dark lettering, or lettering on ink, navy and cobalt. It is never lettering on paper, and lettering on yellow is #111827 in both printings.

rules.name: The Refusal Rule
rules.body: Red appears only where something is refused, blocked or failed. It does not mark emphasis, degrees of warning, or decoration.

rules.name: The Re-pointed Roles Rule
rules.body: A coloured band re-points the role tokens (ink, second ink, rule, link, tint, focus) for everything inside it. Components are not restyled per band; they read the roles.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: XK Display is the lettering of the chart: headlines, part and section titles, signs, plaques and designators. Song is the book being quoted: quoted source text, and inside the book's prose its block quotations and the emphasis that Chinese does not italicise. Monospace names files, commands and identifiers. Nothing else uses any of the three, and the theme's own sentences are never set in Song.

rules.name: The Cut Face Rule
rules.body: XK Display and XK Song are subsets cut to the characters the pages set in them: on the project page its display text, signs, plaques and quoted passage; in the handbook the theme's own strings, the book index and every first- and second-level heading. Anything outside the cut (lesson-written titles, research topics loaded from data, third-level headings, body copy) is set in the body sans. A new display string means re-cutting the subset (`website/scripts/build_page_fonts.py` for the project page, `website/scripts/build_fonts.py` for the handbook); `--check` reports uncovered characters without writing anything.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Counts, dates, lengths and designators use tabular numerals wherever they sit in a column or a strip.

rules.name: The Redraw Rule
rules.body: The plan view and the profile are measured and redrawn at the size they are given, with lettering in fixed pixels: three plan compositions, a profile that sheds names and file labels as it narrows. Figures with a fixed geometry (the roses, the hold) scale as a whole, and on a phone the home rose is reduced to a symbol instead of being shrunk with its numerals.

rules.name: The Flat Band Rule
rules.body: Page-scale colour is a full-width flat field of paper, yellow, ink or cobalt, edge to edge, and everything inside it reads the band's roles.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: If something needs to read as above something else, give it an ink rule and an opaque ground. Shadows, glows and translucent glass are not part of this system.

rules.name: The Square Frame Rule
rules.body: Radius is for controls (3px) and chips (2px). A frame, a strip, a band or a figure with rounded corners is out of system.

rules.name: The Line Style Rule
rules.body: Line style is a statement and is always explained beside the drawing. Solid ink is a required leg or sourced material. Dots (2 on, 7 off) are a leg flown only when needed. Long dashes (9 on, 7 off) in second ink are the go-around. A thick magenta line is the current route, and magenta dots are the lead-in a route takes before its first fix. A fix filled magenta has been flown, outlined in dashed magenta it may be added, outlined in the strong rule it is not on this route. A handoff file ruled above and below must be written; with a dashed underline it is written only when needed. In the handbook a solid ink frame with a filled tag is sourced, a dashed cobalt frame with a dashed tag is assumed for teaching, and a red frame under a red plaque is what may not be inferred.

dos: **Do** put identity, status and navigation data in a ruled strip: 1px gaps over an ink ground inside a 1.5px ink border, label over value.
**Do** let line style carry state, and print the legend or tag that explains it beside the drawing, so no meaning rests on colour alone.
**Do** keep magenta for position, yellow for the sign and red for refusal, and set lettering on yellow in #111827 in both printings.
**Do** re-point the role tokens on a band and let components read them, instead of restyling a component per ground.
**Do** recompose a chart for the space it has, and give every drawing a text twin on the same page: the route table, the fix list, the parts list, the strip board.
**Do** keep the 3px focus outline at 3px offset on every control, in the colour its ground calls for.
**Do** re-cut the display subsets when display text changes, and run the build scripts with `--check` before publishing.
**Do** honour reduced motion with a complete still state: the route painted, the aircraft parked, nothing left half-drawn.
donts: **Don't** add a box-shadow, a text-shadow, a blur or a glow; depth is a rule and a ground.
**Don't** blend colours. Fields are flat; a gradient appears only as a hard-edged drawing device such as the bar under a key sentence or the ticks of a scale.
**Don't** round a frame, a strip, a band or a figure, and don't give a control more than 3px or a chip more than 2px.
**Don't** use magenta as a ground for a band, a button or a heading, yellow as lettering on paper, or red for emphasis.
**Don't** use a dashed or dotted line as decoration; here it means conditional or assumed.
**Don't** set text in XK Display that the cut does not cover (lesson-written titles, data loaded at run time), and don't set the theme's own words in Song.
**Don't** add a label line above a heading. Labels belong inside ruled cells, over the value they name; a heading stands alone.
**Don't** type a character where an icon is meant; icons are stroked drawings on the 24-unit grid.
**Don't** shrink a chart until its lettering stops being readable; recompose it or drop labels.
**Don't** apply these sections to theory sources or to the pages the Skill generates; those are described under Output surfaces.
